utterances.speaker: spk_2
utterances.text: Mossgate Physio, this is Arjun.

utterances.speaker: spk_1
utterances.text: Hi Arjun, it's Sam from Vantrellis. I saw your team finished the Harlow Street job last week. How did that land?

utterances.speaker: spk_2
utterances.text: Ha, it was a sprint, but we got there. Thanks for asking.

utterances.speaker: spk_1
utterances.text: Today I'll walk you through how we work and then show you the product.

utterances.speaker: spk_2
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: spk_1
utterances.text: What's the biggest challenge with cancellations right now?

utterances.speaker: spk_2
utterances.text: It takes too long. Our front desk lead spends two or three hours a day on the phone on it.

utterances.speaker: spk_1
utterances.text: If nothing changes over the next six months, what does that cost you?

utterances.speaker: spk_2
utterances.text: Honestly? Roughly four thousand dollars a week in empty chairs. And people are tired of it.

utterances.speaker: spk_1
utterances.text: What would success look like by the end of the quarter?

utterances.speaker: spk_2
utterances.text: Get cancellations down to under five empty slots a week, and zero missed appointments.

utterances.speaker: spk_1
utterances.text: Let me make sure I have this right. Our front desk lead spends two or three hours a day on the phone on filling last-minute cancellations, and things still slip. Did I miss anything?

utterances.speaker: spk_2
utterances.text: No, that's it exactly.

utterances.speaker: spk_1
utterances.text: You said our front desk lead spends two or three hours a day on the phone on filling last-minute cancellations. With us, open slots go out to the waitlist by text automatically. That's the part that would have caught it when we had eleven empty slots last Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: spk_2
utterances.text: Okay. What does something like that cost?

utterances.speaker: spk_1
utterances.text: It's thirty-six thousand dollars a year.

utterances.speaker: spk_2
utterances.text: That's steep for us.

utterances.speaker: spk_1
utterances.text: I hear you. I could probably do fifteen percent off if that helps.

utterances.speaker: spk_2
utterances.text: Maybe. I'd have to think about it.

utterances.speaker: spk_1
utterances.text: Who else weighs in on a decision like this, and how have you bought software like this before?

utterances.speaker: spk_2
utterances.text: I'd bring in Morgan, our operations director. Morgan signs anything over ten thousand. Last time it took about a month with a trial first.

utterances.speaker: spk_1
utterances.text: So a trial, then Morgan, about a month. Is there a date you'd want this live by?

utterances.speaker: spk_2
utterances.text: Before the busy season, so November.

utterances.speaker: spk_1
utterances.text: Does what you've seen so far make sense for your team?

utterances.speaker: spk_2
utterances.text: Can you just send me some info and I'll look it over?

utterances.speaker: spk_1
utterances.text: Happy to. So I send the right thing, what would you need to see in it?

utterances.speaker: spk_2
utterances.text: Probably proof it works with our current tools, and something I can show Morgan.

utterances.speaker: spk_1
utterances.text: Can we put thirty minutes on the calendar with Morgan for Thursday at ten, so you both see it running with your tools?

utterances.speaker: spk_2
utterances.text: Thursday at ten works. I'll forward the invite to Morgan.

utterances.speaker: spk_1
utterances.text: Thanks Arjun, really appreciate the time.

utterances.speaker: spk_2
utterances.text: Thanks, bye.

Rep does most of the talking in this stretch.
